title: Deferred delete of an array whose ownership was transferred to the catalog (double-free risk)
evidence:
trimmed := make([dynamic]Demand_Entry, 0, 4, context.allocator)
	defer delete(trimmed)
...
	delete(e3.entries)
	e3.entries = trimmed ... defer catalogs_destroy(cat2)
detail: After e3.entries = trimmed, the deferred delete(trimmed) frees memory catalogs_destroy(cat2) will also free; double-free if the destroy frees demand entries, leak otherwise. Ownership transfer is unmarked.
recommended_fix: Drop `defer delete(trimmed)` once ownership passes to cat2 (it is freed via catalogs_destroy), or copy entries in place instead of reassigning.

title: W9 'growth must place >= 8' assertion is trivially satisfied by the seeded fixture
evidence:
host_pos := [8][2]i32{{8, 10}, {12, 8}, {16, 6}, {24, 6}, {28, 8}, {32, 10}, {36, 12}, {34, 20}}
	for hp in host_pos { topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, host_idx, hp, cat) } ... testing.expectf(t, hosts >= 8, "growth must place >= 8 streaming-capable terminals (content_hosts + campuses) by the surge window (got %d) — the aggregation crowd", hosts)
detail: The seed map places 14 streaming-capable terminals at tick 0, so hosts >= 8 cannot fail and the 'growth must place' message contradicts the fixture; the original growth-builds-the-crowd validation is silently discarded.
recommended_fix: Either assert on growth-spawned nodes only, or reword the message to match the seeded crowd; state explicitly that growth placement is no longer under test.

title: 'campus half is fully served' comment overstates the ≥W*9/10 floor
evidence:
// the campus half is fully served (the flood) over the whole run
	testing.expectf(t, total_campus >= W*9/10,
detail: One campus caps at 2.5/tick against a 10/tick surge ask (10x vol on the campus entry); the 1800 floor is ~36% of the cap-time ceiling — 'fully served' is not what is asserted.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment to match the assertion (a volume floor), or compute the floor against the campus's actual cap-time ceiling.

title: Surge window derived from the set-piece in W9 but hardcoded 1200 in the new profile test
evidence:
SURGE_AT :: u64(1200) // the streaming surge's data start_tick ... surge := &cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0]
	SURGE_START := u64(surge.start_tick)
detail: W9 derives its window explicitly so 'a future re-tune of the surge timing cannot silently drift this pin'; the sibling test in the same PR hardcodes 1200, so a re-tune silently mis-bins its base/surge split and weakens the ratio pins.
recommended_fix: Derive SURGE_AT from the same set_piece (start_tick) in test_terminal_class_profiles.

title: W9 header still says 'era-3 demand 1+1' while asserting the doubled 20/tick ask
detail: Within one comment block, era-3 demand is described as '1+1' while the same block states the roster doubles it (two streaming entries, 20/tick). The '1+1' parenthetical is stale after 5.11.
recommended_fix: Update the parenthetical to the current totals (email 2 entries / streaming 2 entries) or mark it as the historical 5.9 re-tune.
